paragraphs.source_en: Mariner 8’s failure had also been caused by something small, an integrated-circuit chip, no bigger than a sunflower seed. A faulty diode had likely failed to protect it from a voltage surge. The Mariner 9 engineers persevered through the rest of May after happening upon a second issue: a short in the propellant system. They hurriedly pulled the spacecraft down from the Centaur, fixed it, then reran a full set of tests. Finally, NASA got the spacecraft back on top of its rocket. On May 30, on a clear blue evening, Mariner 9 lifted into the sky, joining the race to make the first full map of Mars.
